missing: The actual dollar math: savings per cycle given the peak/off-peak price gap, round-trip efficiency losses and the cost of wearing down the battery, plus payback years for specific stations at current prices. Without this, a shopper can't tell whether a given station would ever pay for itself.
why: One major reviewer answers this exact question from hands-on use: Popular Mechanics, which also shows up twice more as copies on Yahoo and AOL. It names stations that have a TOU mode, but admits the savings are hard to estimate and gives no figures. The utility and government pages explain TOU rates but say nothing about power stations, and Palmetto only says savings are "modest." A page that does the cost-per-cycle and payback math for each station could get in and win citations. It would still compete with Popular Mechanics, which fills three result slots.
